newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares dip, Boehler weighs.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares dip, Boehler weighs.

text.p: Austria's ATX index finished slightly lower on Thursday, knocked from its recent upward path by selling in highgrade steelmaker Boehler-Uddeholm and other heavy-weight stocks.
The blue-chip ATX closed 2.92 points, or 0.23 percent, down at 1,287.19. Nevertheless, market participants said the underlying tone remained positive.
"Today was merely a pause. There was a bit of pressure from the debt market and that was exacerbated by Boehler and Lenzing," a trader said.
Overall eight shares finished higher and 13 lower.
Boehler-Uddholm was the leading decliner on brisk turnover. It shed 21 schillings, or 2.35 percent, to end at 905.2 schillings after reporting a drop in first quarter earnings.
Analysts forecast a speedy recovery in the share price, however, and noted that comparative figures for the first quarter of 1996 had been extraordinarily strong.

"It is significant that order intake was up four percent in the first quarter and 37 percent in April. I expect the second half of 1997 to be much better," said Alfred Reisenberger, an analyst at IMI Sigeco.

Fibre maker Lenzing slumped to a low of 681 schillings after the firm said it had swung into red figures last year and was scrapping its dividend. The stock later recovered to close at 691, 8.9 schillings down on the day.
Among the few gainers were Bank Austria preferred shares and chip maker AMS.
June ATX future stood 4.5 points down at 1,284.5. The broad-based Vienna bourse index was 0.86 points down at 473.65. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 531 12256
